content: Engaging in moderate-intensity physical activity, such as brisk walking for a minimum of 150 minutes per week, is highly beneficial for individuals at risk of developing type 2 diabetes as well as those diagnosed with prediabetes. This level of physical activity has been shown to enhance insulin sensitivity and reduce abdominal fat in both children and adults, which are critical factors in diabetes prevention. Interrupting prolonged periods of sedentary behavior and incorporating resistance training into one’s routine provide additional advantages in lowering the risk of diabetes. These strategies not only improve metabolic health but also contribute to better overall glucose regulation. Furthermore, regular physical activity has been demonstrated to play a significant role in preventing gestational diabetes in pregnant women, thereby promoting healthier outcomes for both the mother and the baby.
